crime: Every evening in the courtyard, a prisoner stood on the fountain rim with her teacup and roasted one of the girls. {WITCH_NAME} stood up there beside her, and on every punchline she took a pratfall off the rim, hit the stones and bounced back to her feet like a rubber ball.
One evening, between falls, the roaster froze her face into {WITCH_NAME}'s blank stare. "And this," she said, "is her choosing which of us to hold under."

At seven, {WITCH_NAME} had pictured holding her baby brother under the bathwater. She lifted him out, threw herself down on the wet tiles, and the whole house laughed. "While they're laughing," she said, "I'm not the girl who would do it."
That evening she stood on the rim and did not fall. The prisoners laughed anyway.

After the others went in, the roaster stayed behind alone, rinsing her teacup at the fountain as she did every night. {WITCH_NAME} walked back, pushed the roaster's head under the water and held it there until she was still. The teacup dropped from her hand and bounced, whole, on the stone path.

Before lockup, the prisoners found the roaster face down in the fountain, her teacup shattered on the path beside the rim. In the trial court they ruled {WITCH_NAME} out: no cup that fell within a few steps of her could break.

Then one prisoner gathered the shards. They had been pressed flat in a star around a heel print in fine powder. The prisoners understood. The cup had never broken in the fall. It had bounced whole beside {WITCH_NAME}, and she had stamped on it.
fields.epitaph: Nothing that fell near her ever broke, only what she held down.
fields.epithet: A clown afraid of her own hands
execution: The execution stand raised a tower of dining-hall plates and cups to the ceiling. She knelt beneath it, chained to the stone floor.
The tower tipped, and the china poured down around her. Every plate and cup struck the floor whole and bounced straight back up into her.
On every rebound they struck her head and shoulders again. Her head jerked with each blow, until it hung.
Bounce by bounce, the china fell lower and settled around her, unbroken. She lay still, the only broken thing on the floor.

magic.name: Bounce Back
magic.text: People and things that fall near her bounce off the ground like rubber balls, unharmed.
